issues.t: Engine stalling from loose harness connectors
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving, sometimes over bumps or when the engine rocks on its mounts, and may restart normally afterward.
issues.why: Engine movement could tug on the wiring harness and work two connectors loose, breaking the circuit. Kia recalled these trucks to lock the connectors with clips and splice the harness.
issues.next: Avoid driving until a VIN recall check confirms the harness repair was done. If it stalls, get off the road safely and have it towed for inspection.

issues.sym: The belt seems to click in but pulls free with a firm tug, or releases unexpectedly.
issues.why: The buckle could appear latched without fully locking the tongue. Kia recalled the buckles, and NHTSA later reopened the issue with a recall query.
issues.next: Tug on every belt after buckling. Have a Kia dealer confirm the buckle recall was completed, and replace any buckle that releases.

issues.t: Rear brake line can rub through
issues.sym: Brake fluid drips near a rear wheel, the brake warning light comes on, or the pedal sinks lower than normal.
issues.why: A rear brake pipe had too little clearance from nearby parts and could chafe until it leaked, reducing rear braking.
issues.next: Do not drive with a low or soft pedal. Have the rear brake lines inspected and confirm the recall repair on your VIN.

issues.t: Fuel leaking from the tank or filler area
issues.sym: Strong gas smell, or fuel spilling or dripping under the vehicle, often while filling up.
issues.why: Owners widely reported fuel tank and filler leaks on these trucks, and NHTSA opened investigations into fuel tank leakage. Age and rust on the tank, filler neck and lines make it worse.
issues.next: Do not drive or park in a garage if you smell or see fuel. Have the tank, filler neck and lines inspected and leaking parts replaced.

issues.sym: Brake lights stay dark or stay on, the shifter will not leave Park, cruise control does not cancel with the brake, or the stability control light comes on.
issues.why: The switch at the brake pedal could wear or malfunction. Kia recalled it twice: once for earlier trucks and again for a wider range of years.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights while you press the pedal, and look up open recalls on your VIN. A dealer replaces the switch.

issues.sym: Often no warning. Rusted straps may let the tank rattle or sag under the rear of the vehicle.
issues.why: Kia set up a product improvement program to replace the fuel tank support straps on trucks built from mid-2004 to early 2007.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer whether program PI1801 applies to your VIN, and have the straps checked for rust at your next service.

issues.sym: Water drips from the headliner or sunroof edge after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: On earlier production trucks the sunroof glass did not seal properly against its weatherstrip. Kia issued a glass adjustment procedure.
issues.next: Clear the sunroof drains first. If it still leaks, ask a dealer about bulletin PS075R1.

issues.sym: A droning or humming from underneath at low to moderate city speeds on 4WD models.
issues.why: A bearing in the 4WD coupling can bind or become damaged. Kia published a bulletin for diagnosing and repairing it.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm where the noise comes from and reference Kia bulletin TSB-023.

issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay, sometimes with the ABS light on, and it can happen with the vehicle parked and off.
issues.why: Moisture or brake fluid can get into the ABS hydraulic control unit and short its circuit board. The 2008-2009 trucks were recalled twice, and later years were added in a large Hyundai-Kia recall.
issues.next: Run a VIN recall check now. Park outside and away from buildings until the repair is done, and stop driving if you see smoke.

issues.t: Rod bearing failure and engine seizure
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, a flashing check engine light, oil warning, sudden power loss or stalling. Some engines have caught fire after failing.
issues.why: Machining debris could restrict oil flow to the connecting rod bearings, which then wear and seize. Kia recalled affected engines and a class settlement added extended engine coverage once the knock sensing software is installed.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine knocks or the check engine light flashes. Check your VIN for open recalls and confirm the knock-detection software update was done.

issues.sym: Engine knock, a flashing check engine light, or loss of power.
issues.why: The port-injected 2.4L in these years has the same bearing wear risk. Kia added a knock sensing software campaign and these engines were brought into a later engine settlement.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine knocks. Ask a Kia dealer to confirm campaign PI2103 and your extended engine coverage.

issues.sym: Gas smell in or around the vehicle, especially after an engine replacement.
issues.why: On some trucks that received a replacement engine, the high-pressure fuel pipe could be left improperly installed and leak fuel near hot engine parts.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and have it towed. Check your VIN for this recall if the engine was ever replaced.

issues.sym: Low oil warning or needing to add oil between changes, sometimes with blue smoke at startup.
issues.why: Kia issued a bulletin for diagnosing oil consumption on its four-cylinder engine families, and oil burning is the top complaint for some years such as 2017. Running low on oil also raises bearing failure risk on these engines.
issues.next: Check the oil level every few fill-ups and keep it full. Ask a dealer for an oil consumption test under bulletin ENG222 and keep records.

issues.sym: Signs of break-in such as a broken rear window or damaged steering column, or the vehicle going missing.
issues.why: Key-start trims were built without an engine immobilizer, so thieves learned to start them without the key. Kia released a free anti-theft software upgrade and ignition cylinder protector.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer for the free anti-theft software update (CS2302) and the ignition protector, and consider a steering wheel lock.

issues.t: Column power steering clunk or failure
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking felt through the steering wheel, steering that feels heavy or notchy, or a power steering warning light.
issues.why: These Sportages use an electric motor on the steering column. Its coupling, worm gear, motor or control unit can wear or fail, and Kia issued a bulletin allowing partial repairs instead of replacing the whole column.
issues.next: Have the steering checked soon, especially if it gets heavy. Ask the shop about Kia bulletin CHA084.

issues.sym: Check engine or AWD warning light on, and the rear wheels no longer help in slippery conditions.
issues.why: The hydraulic actuator in the AWD coupling can fail. Kia issued a bulletin to replace it.
issues.next: Have the AWD codes read and ask about Kia bulletin TSBCHA047. Keep all four tires matched in size and wear.

issues.t: Inhibitor switch causes no-start or rough shifts
issues.sym: The engine will not crank in Park, or the transmission shifts unevenly.
issues.why: The transmission range (inhibitor) switch could shift out of position. Kia added a bracket to hold it in place.
issues.next: Try starting in Neutral as a temporary check, then have a dealer inspect the switch under bulletin TSB-044.

issues.t: Low fuel pressure code on 2.0 turbo
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0087, sometimes with hesitation or reduced power.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel system on the turbo engine could report low pressure. Kia issued a computer update and, where needed, replacement of the high-pressure pump, pipe and bolts.
issues.next: Have the code read and ask a dealer about campaign SC114 and bulletin TSB-FUE026.

issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P2562 or P2565, sometimes with weak boost.
issues.why: The turbo's electric wastegate actuator could lose its adjustment. Kia issued a computer reflash and actuator adjustment.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a dealer about bulletin ENG130.

issues.sym: Smoke or a burning or melting smell from the engine bay, or ABS and tire pressure warning lights, even while parked.
issues.why: A circuit in the ABS hydraulic control unit can short and overheat. Kia recalled these trucks to change fuses and, on some, update software.
issues.next: Run a VIN recall check. Park outside and away from buildings until the recall fix is done, and stop driving if you notice smoke.

issues.t: Tow hitch wiring module fire risk
issues.sym: Burning smell or smoke near the rear of the vehicle, or a blown fuse, on trucks with a tow hitch harness.
issues.why: Dirt and moisture can reach the circuit board in the trailer wiring module and cause a short that can start a fire, whether the harness was factory or dealer installed.
issues.next: If your truck has a tow hitch harness, check your VIN for this recall and park outside until it is fixed.

issues.t: Door will not open from outside
issues.sym: Pulling the outside door handle does nothing, though the door may still open from inside unless child locks are on.
issues.why: The door latches on some trucks can stop working properly. Kia extended warranty coverage on the latches.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer about warranty extension WTY020 and have any sticking latch replaced.

issues.sym: The airbag light stays on after startup.
issues.why: Kia found faults with the airbag control unit on some trucks and extended warranty coverage for the related repairs.
issues.next: Have the airbag system scanned promptly. Ask a dealer about warranty extension WTY027 and bulletin ELE254.

issues.sym: No-start in Park, a wrong gear shown on the dash, or harsh or odd shifting.
issues.why: Kia issued bulletins to replace the transmission range switch on some of these trucks.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the switch and reference bulletin TRA072.

issues.sym: Sudden stall, flickering lights, or a burning smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: The nut on the alternator's battery cable terminal could work loose, causing stalling or an electrical surge that can start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall SC248 and get it fixed before driving much further.

issues.sym: Burning smell or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: The controller for the electric transmission oil pump used by the idle stop and go system can have damaged parts and overheat.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and park outside away from buildings until the pump controller is replaced.

issues.sym: A hard brake pedal that takes much more effort, longer stops, and sometimes a check engine light for a lean condition.
issues.why: The diaphragm inside the brake booster can slip out of place and leak vacuum, removing power assist.
issues.next: If the pedal suddenly feels hard, stop driving and have it towed. Check your VIN for recall SC272.

issues.sym: The gauge display goes dark, hiding speed, warning lights and tire pressure alerts.
issues.why: Kia recalled these trucks because the cluster display could fail to show information.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the dealer update or replace the cluster.

issues.sym: Usually no warning. Sometimes an airbag warning light.
issues.why: An airbag on some trucks could be folded or twisted during assembly, so it may not deploy correctly in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the dealer inspect the airbag.

issues.sym: Wind noise, flapping or rattling from the roof, or a molding strip lifting at the edge.
issues.why: The roof trim molding may not be secured well enough and can detach at speed, creating a hazard for other drivers.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the molding is lifting, have it secured before highway driving.

issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often with a power steering warning light.
issues.why: A circuit board in the electric power steering unit can short, cutting assist.
issues.next: Steering will still work but takes much more effort. Drive only as needed to get it repaired and check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Gauge screen failure with tow hitch harness
issues.sym: The instrument screen goes blank, hiding speed and warning lights.
issues.why: A software error in the tow hitch harness control module can make the instrument screen fail. This affects plug-in hybrids and some trucks with the smaller gauge screen and a Kia tow harness.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Dealers replace the tow hitch harness control module.
